payload.name: Preserve distinct event memories
payload.description: When a new message mentions an event that is a different occurrence from an existing event memory (different ordinal, date, or instance), ADD a new memory instead of UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE.
content: During extraction, if a new candidate event is similar to an existing event memory but clearly represents a different occurrence (e.g., 'first' vs 'fourth' win, distinct dates, separate instances), create a new memory (ADD) and do not overwrite the existing one.

Before choosing UPDATE, verify that the incoming information revises or corrects the same fact/entity state. If it introduces an additional distinct event, always use ADD. Preserve the original event memory unchanged.
Do not merge two distinct events into a single memory even if they share subject or activity; keep each event with its own timestamp and content.

solves: When constructing memories from a conversation, a later message may describe a different occurrence of a similar event (e.g., a fourth win vs. an earlier first win). The agent must recognize that distinct events, even if thematically related, are separate memories and must not overwrite or merge an existing event memory with a new one. This abstract rule prevents the loss of historical facts and applies to any repeated or reiterated event type.
